transcript.text: Hi everyone. The public API rate-limit project is ready for its production policy review on August 25, and I'll be making the final decision on the policy that gets communicated to customers. Before I record anything, I need to hear from each of the relevant teams — backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations — on any release-impacting findings you have. Once I record the final policy, each affected team will also need to record the operational commitment associated with its finding, including any escalation or handoff required for launch support. Let's go through the draft policy: it currently allows 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, applies the same limit to authentication endpoints, and does not specify a staffed launch window. I'd like to hear your findings and concerns so we can finalize this properly.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Backend's load replay shows the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. I have not updated the policy draft because the client test was owned by another team.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a customer-impacting finding. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that its contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered the clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this is something we need to account for before the policy is finalized and communicated.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a security finding from a credential-abuse investigation I was running this afternoon. I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key — not the 100 requests per minute currently in the draft policy. This is critical because applying the higher 100 rpm limit to auth endpoints would leave them vulnerable to credential-stuffing attacks. The finding isn't in the security tracker yet because the investigation is still being closed, but I wanted to surface it now before the policy is finalized.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a support operations finding. We confirmed today that the staffed launch team is available only from exactly 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15, with an escalation handoff documented for that window. I haven't added the coverage block to the launch plan yet because scheduling approval finished after the plan was circulated, but this is our committed launch support window and it aligns with the September 15 enforcement date Carlos mentioned.
